builder_plan.scenario: An agent reads external documents or tool responses that may contain malicious instructions.
builder_plan.change: Replay attacks and legitimate lookalikes in an isolated copy of your agent workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your existing checks with the same tasks, permissions, and tool responses.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful attacks missed, legitimate actions blocked, detection delay, and review cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: MINE: A Training-Free Defense against Indirect Prompt Injection via Mutual Information and Embedding Variance
summary: MINE replaces prompt-engineering defenses and supervised injection detectors with a training-free, query-conditioned reranking of retrieved content based on mutual information and embedding variance, defending by maximizing relevance rather than detecting attacks. It costs an additional reranking computation per query over retrieved chunks (embedding and mutual-information estimation, implementable with small models or APIs), adding modest latency that the paper claims is lower than competing defenses on long contexts. It can fail against attacks whose injected instructions remain highly query-relevant, against attackers who optimize directly against the mutual-information criterion beyond the evaluated adaptive setting, and when the embedding model used for scoring differs from the deployment stack, since the reported results depend on specific benchmarks and embedding choices.
rationale: The method is training-free, API-compatible, and incurs no retraining or infrastructure cost, but its security benefit must be validated on the reader's own retrieval pipeline and threat model before production reliance.
technique: Training-free indirect prompt injection defense via relevance reranking

claims.statement: MINE replaces prompt-engineering defenses and supervised injection detectors with a training-free, query-conditioned reranking of retrieved content based on mutual information and embedding variance, defending by maximizing relevance rather than detecting attacks. It costs an additional reranking computation per query over retrieved chunks (embedding and mutual-information estimation, implementable with small models or APIs), adding modest latency that the paper claims is lower than competing defenses on long contexts. It can fail against attacks whose injected instructions remain highly query-relevant, against attackers who optimize directly against the mutual-information criterion beyond the evaluated adaptive setting, and when the embedding model used for scoring differs from the deployment stack, since the reported results depend on specific benchmarks and embedding choices.

MINE achieves the best accuracy-security trade-off among training-free defenses across four benchmarks (Inj-SQuAD, Inj-TriviaQA, LC-Inj-SQuAD, InjecAgent), remains usable against a fully adaptive attacker, and has the lowest inference latency among compared defenses on long contexts; no multiplicative numeric factor is reported in the abstract.
